title: Rep Range Compass
user: A strength trainee using double progression who needs to know the next set's target and whether a weight increase is earned, without moving their health history to a hosted service.

evidence.quote_or_summary: In the self-hosted workout-tracker discussion, users call out missing Apple Health import, unclear current-set position, and incomplete mobile workflow.
A user explains that common 3×8–12 double progression cannot be represented because a weight increase fires after the bottom of the range rather than all sets reaching the top.

recurrence: Two independent fitness-tracker communities identify the same high-frequency moment: recording a set while deciding whether to progress. It occurs every workout for lifters using rep ranges.
current_workaround: Use a full workout tracker plus a notes field, spreadsheet, or mental arithmetic to remember rep-range state.
incumbents_and_gap: wger, Hevy, Strong, and Ryot record workouts, but their broad programs obscure the narrow next-set/next-weight decision and can require an account or server.
smallest_useful_product: Offline PWA with one exercise card: log weight/reps/RIR, apply a configurable rep-range rule, show the next-set cue and export/import CSV. Non-goals: exercise library, social feed, coaching, nutrition, or medical metrics.
success_measure: In a four-week pilot, 70% of users log at least eight sessions and can answer 'increase or repeat?' without a separate note in 90% of logged exercises.
monetization: one-time — a focused personal log should keep data local and not make training history contingent on a subscription.
constraints: All data stays in IndexedDB by default; CSV import must be local; clearly state that progression suggestions are configurable arithmetic, not coaching or medical advice.
why_distinct: It is a progression decision card, not another full workout catalogue or AI fitness coach.
